reason: Next.js 15.5.20 vendors its own internal postcss@8.4.31 inside node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss. Verified directly: an npm `overrides` entry does not remove this nested copy (Node module resolution still finds Next's own bundled version from within Next's own code), and forcing the override produces an invalid npm dependency tree (`ELSPROBLEMS`) for no actual security benefit. The XSS is in postcss's CSS stringifier and requires attacker-controlled CSS content reaching postcss; this project's own build pipeline only processes static, repository-authored Tailwind source files. Waiting on an upstream Next.js patch release that bumps its internal postcss pin.

Next.js 15.5.24 vendors its own postcss@8.4.31 at node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss; the workspace's own postcss is 8.5.26 and already patched. The nested copy cannot be removed by an npm `overrides` entry (see the GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 waiver, where that was verified directly), and `npm audit fix --force` resolves it only by installing next@16.3.3, a major upgrade out of scope for a dependency-refresh pass. Reachability: postcss runs here only at build time, over first-party Tailwind and CSS sources in apps/web that are authored in this repository. No untrusted or user-supplied stylesheet reaches it, and the emitted CSS is static. This advisory is arbitrary file read via postcss's handling of a crafted stylesheet, which requires attacker-controlled CSS input.
